name: Pencil Hall of Mirrors
description: A graphite corridor remembers itself in four looking glasses. Walk between recursive reflections, then find the room beyond the room.

assets.credit: Original projected linework from the procedural mirror hall
Three.js contributors · reflection-camera and oblique-clipping reference

compatibility: WebGL2 with a bundled Three.js runtime in the standalone export. Unsupported devices receive a labeled static plate. Low quality uses a single reflection rather than recursion.
Native wheel, trackpad, touch and keyboard scrolling. A timeline can seek any position. Pointer inspection is opt-in; touch inspection uses dragging and the timeline.
Rendering is demand-driven and stops when settled, paused, hidden or offscreen. Reduced motion starts paused; manual timeline changes remain available.
Up to four recursive levels and 16 reflection passes, with smaller targets at deeper levels. Adaptive mode reduces resolution and, if necessary, falls back to one bounce.
A fixed vertical camera avoids roll. All journey positions are sampled from normalized progress; reverse scrolling reconstructs the same world and camera.
notes: This is real three-dimensional linework: columns, doorway arches, beams, perspective grids, engraved mirror frames and small gear mechanisms. Strokes are seeded and batched by weight.
Each mirror projects a separately rendered reflected-camera view. Opposing mirrors use bounded recursive passes, oblique clipping at the mirror plane and unique targets within each frame.
Reflections fade toward paper as depth increases. The frame graph shares a fixed pass budget across visible mirrors and terminates deeper views on a quiet ivory surface.
Parallel mirrors and the angled maze use physical planar reflection transforms. The Impossible Gallery adds one explicitly labeled artistic portal mapped to a different architectural chamber.

The journey begins outside, enters the hall, turns toward the looking glasses and reaches another chamber. Gallery passage is spatially registered across the portal; it is not presented as a physically possible mirror.
Sketch density and hatching direction rebuild the architectural linework. Brightness, fading and recursion change the reflection system itself. Camera position changes actual parallax.
reuse: Serve the exported ZIP over local HTTP and open example.html; the exact Three.js runtime and MIT licenses are included.
Use createReflectionSystem(renderer, scene) independently with your own geometry, mirror definitions and camera. See embed-demo.html for an isolated two-mirror example.
Use createHallViewer for the complete corridor, or sampleJourney for an independently controlled scroll timeline.
README.md documents plane orientation, target budgets, portal distinctions, schemas, render ordering, cleanup and browser limitations.
